**Triage: first-touch grading** — `pm:queue` · `domain:spec` · `priority:p2` · **`pm:blocking`**. ⛔ No type label — see below. Readings taken in THIS act, 2026-09-20T08:49Z. <sub>本评论来自分诊座位</sub>

**This is a cross-repo reading request, and it is in the right repo.** It asks the lane that owns the **producer** three questions about the permission-set provenance predicate, and it exists because objectui#5987's body forbids the failure it would otherwise cause: 「⛔ do not guess the provenance predicate from the current row shape」.

**Lane `domain:spec`**: the predicate is a contract question (which projection field a consumer may key a lock on) and `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` lives in the error-code ledger, `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`. ⚠️ Questions (1) and (3) are **runtime** readings the filing seat explicitly could not take — if answering them turns out to require standing up the producer rather than reading the contract, that half belongs to `domain:services`/`domain:engine` and the spec seat should say so rather than guess.

**`pm:blocking` applied, derivation re-run here**: **objectui#5987** reads `open` · `pm:blocked` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui`, and its **body** carries `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#19195`. ⇒ one open downstream depender naming this card through the machine-readable carrier. ⭐ It is described as the **oldest p2 product card in that lane and otherwise ready** — so this reading is the only thing between a finished UI card and a dispatch.

**`priority:p2`**, inherited from what it unblocks rather than invented: nothing here is broken, and the deliverable is a **measurement**. ⛔ **No `bug` / `enhancement` label**: the type test asks whether a declared contract is violated (Bug) or the accepted set widens (Feature), and a reading request is neither — it is the Task arm, for which this board has no label. ⇒ left unset deliberately, ⛔ not overlooked.

⚠️ ⭐ The filer already did the part it could and **marked the boundary**: it took the ledger counts with a control (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE` 7/7 across 17.3.0 and 17.4.0, control `package_id` 18/18) and ⛔ **did not attempt (1) or (3)**, naming them as runtime readings it could not stand up. ⇒ the answering seat starts from a partial reading, not from zero, and ⛔ should not re-take the ledger half.

---

## (1) What does a UI reader actually receive?

**Instrument.** `GET /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set?limit=200` over the cookie session — the ordinary data door, end to end. ⛔ Not a direct call to a projection function with `isSystem: true`; the two are different readings and only this one answers the card.

**Reading — SERVED, in full, unmasked.** `total: 17`, `records: 17`, and **17/17 rows carry every provenance column**:

```
key union over the 17 records (key: rows carrying it)
  active 17        customized 17      drift_detail 17   drift_status 17
  managed_by 17    package_id 17      organization_id 17
  admin_scope 17   created_at 17      created_by 17     description 17
  field_permissions 17   id 17        label 17          name 17
  object_permissions 17  row_level_security 17
  system_permissions 17  tab_permissions 17
  updated_at 17    updated_by 17
```

Values, non-null and un-stripped: 8 rows `managed_by:'platform'` / `package_id:null`, 9 rows `managed_by:'package'` / `package_id:'com.example.showcase'`. `customized` is `false` and `drift_status` is `null` on all 17 (a clean boot, no overlays). The **write response image carries them too** — a `POST` to the same object answered `201` with `managed_by`, `package_id`, `customized`, `drift_status`, `drift_detail` all present.

**Why it comes out that way.** Field-level masking only runs when a permission set declares field permissions for the object (`security-plugin.ts`, step 4 of the security middleware: `maskResults` is called only `if (Object.keys(fieldPerms).length > 0 || Object.keys(partialRules).length > 0)`). Nothing declares any on `sys_permission_set`, so no key is removed. The object itself declares all five columns and its `all_permsets` list view already names `managed_by` / `customized` / `drift_status` as grid columns.

**What would have made it come out differently.** Any permission set granting an explicit non-readable field permission on these columns for the caller. Note the failure mode for the UI: FLS **deletes the key**, it does not null it. ⇒ ⛔ objectui must not read "key absent" as "environment-authored"; absent means "not authorized to know".

**⭐ ZONE-2 ASSUMPTION 4 IS FALSIFIED.** `permission-set-projection.test.ts:285` does **not** iterate the served column list. It iterates the same column *names* in the **opposite direction** — row into metadata body — and asserts they must **NOT** appear:

```ts
it('drops `active` and every other storage column from the projected body', () => {
  const body = permissionSetBodyFromRow(legacyRow());
  for (const col of ['active', 'managed_by', 'package_id', 'customized', …]) {
    expect(body, …).not.toHaveProperty(col);
```

An assertion added there answers a different question. The card's 「may be one assertion away」 cost estimate was wrong, and standing up the real door was required — exactly as the dispatch cautioned.

---

## (2) Which predicate may a UI lock on?

**Instrument.** A three-column cross-tab over every row: (a) the data-door row's `managed_by` / `package_id`; (b) `item._packageId` from `GET /api/v1/meta/permission/NAME`; (c) **the server's actual verdict** for `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set/ID` with a one-field body.

| name | `managed_by` | `package_id` | meta `_packageId` | PATCH | `code` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| admin_full_access | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| organization_admin | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| organization_admin_no_bypass | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| member_default | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| viewer_readonly | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| mcp_agent_data_read | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| mcp_agent_data_write | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| mcp_agent_restricted | platform | null | com.objectstack.plugin-security | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| showcase_contributor … showcase_client_liaison (9 rows) | package | com.example.showcase | com.example.showcase | **403** | NOT_OVERRIDABLE |
| probe_env_set_19195 (created by this probe) | admin | null | — (absent) | **200** | — |

```
rows total                        : 18
server REFUSES the write (403)    : 17
predicate managed_by === 'package': 9   MISSES 8 of 17 locked rows
predicate package_id present      : 9   MISSES the same 8
predicate meta._packageId present : 17  MISSES 0 · FALSE-LOCKS 0
```

**⛔ LIT CONTROL, so the 403s are about the predicate and not about a closed door:** `POST` of a new set answered **201**, `PATCH` of that same set answered **200**, and `DELETE` of it answered 200 and really removed it (18 rows became 17). The door accepts writes.

**Reading — NEITHER row column is the predicate, and `managed_by` fails LIVE on a default boot.** The card already measured `package_id` wrong. This round measures `managed_by` wrong too, and not only in the field-reported `provenance_skip` shape: **8 of the 17 locked rows (47%) are `managed_by:'platform'`**, because `com.objectstack.plugin-security` ships them as artifacts. A UI locking on `managed_by === 'package'` would render all eight as editable and collect a 403 on every save.

**The server's actual predicate** is `classifyPackagedPermissionSet` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`): *does an installed package declare this name*, read from the engine SchemaRegistry (`ql.registry.listItems('permission')`), skipping the `_envProjection` echo and the `sys_metadata` runtime-shadow sentinel, fail-closed on `unknown`. Its own header states both failure directions of the column, and this round confirms the too-narrow one by execution. `permission-set-overlay-discard.ts` decides eligibility the same way and pins the confounded shape (`managed_by:'admin'` on a genuinely package-declared set) in its own test — **ZONE-2 ASSUMPTION 3 CONFIRMED**.

⇒ **That predicate is a REGISTRY fact. No column on `sys_permission_set` carries it, and none is derivable from the row.**

### ⭐ The predicate objectui CAN key on, measured

`GET /api/v1/meta/permission` — one call, no per-row fan-out — returns **all 18 items** with the provenance envelope, and it includes environment-authored sets (`_packageId: null`), so a join by `name` covers the whole list:

```
showcase_contributor          _packageId='com.example.showcase'            _provenance='package'
organization_admin            _packageId='com.objectstack.plugin-security'  _provenance='package'
probe_env_set_b_19195         _packageId=null                              _provenance=null
```

```
locked := item._packageId is present AND item._packageId is not the string 'sys_metadata'
```

Measured against the server's own verdict: **17/17 locked, 1/1 editable, 0 misses, 0 false locks.**

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED — the `'sys_metadata'` clause.** It is read from source (`declaredPackageIdOf` / `RUNTIME_SHADOW_PACKAGE_ID` in `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`), **not** from a live row: no `_packageId === 'sys_metadata'` item existed on this boot, and minting one now requires an ADR-0086 P2 package publish — the lock itself refuses minting an overlay on a declared name. Keep the clause (it is the lock's own too-broad guard) but treat it as unverified on the wire.

**What would have made (2) come out differently.** If the eight platform sets had not been artifact-declared, `managed_by === 'package'` would have scored 9/9 on this corpus and looked correct. They are declared by `com.objectstack.plugin-security`, which is what turns the lock header's stated risk into a reproduced reading.

**ZONE-2 assumption 1 — CONFIRMED, with line drift.** The admin-door gate does key on `managed_by === 'package'`, but at **`security-plugin.ts:5588`-`:5604`** (card said `:5591`-`:5604`); the update/delete deferral comment is **`:5543`-`:5554`** (card said `:5544`-`:5551`). Text matched, anchors moved.

**ZONE-2 assumption 2 — CONFIRMED for `update`, FALSIFIED for `delete`.** `update` is indeed refused by the downstream producer, not the gate (403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE above). `delete` is **not refused at all** — see finding A.

---

## (3) Is the refusal legible to a UI?

**Instrument.** The raw REST body of each refused write, read as bytes.

**Reading — YES, machine-readable, on a top-level field.** Data door:

```
PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set/ps_…   →  HTTP 403
{"error":"[Security] Permission set 'showcase_contributor' is declared by package 'com.example.showcase' and is locked in this environment — editing it here would silently fork it … Clone it instead (the \"Clone\" action …)","code":"NOT_OVERRIDABLE","object":"sys_permission_set"}
```

Metadata door `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/showcase_contributor` answers the **same** 403 and the **same** `"code":"NOT_OVERRIDABLE"` — one spelling, two doors, as `packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts` claims.

`code` is a sibling of `error`, not a substring of it. ⇒ objectui item 3 is implementable as `error.code === 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'`, rendering the `error` prose as the guidance body — the message already names the clone path. ⛔ No string-matching required, and none should be added.

**Controls.**
- *Discriminating, not constant:* an unauthenticated `PATCH` on the same URL answers `401 {"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","code":"UNAUTHENTICATED",…}` — a different code at a different status.
- *Registered on today's tree:* `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` is a member of the ledger at **`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:624`** at `f93beea` (the card read `:612` — 12 lines of drift). Occurrence count over `packages/spec/src`: `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` **7**; **CONTROL** `package_id`, same corpus and query form, **16**. The zero is lit.

**What would have made (3) come out differently.** If the refusal had opened with `[Security] Access denied`. That prefix is a matcher (`isPermissionDeniedError`, `mapDataError`, `rest-server`'s sanitiser) and would have re-flattened the code to `PERMISSION_DENIED` on the wire. The lock's message deliberately does not — and the measured body proves the avoidance works.

### ⚠️ Two legibility gaps measured on adjacent arms, both of which the UI will hit

**A — `DELETE` on a package-declared set answers `200 {"success":true}` and changes nothing.** Reproduced twice:

```
BEFORE : id=ps_mu9o9o6uybbit6th name=showcase_manager managed_by=package updated_at=2026-09-20T10:27:17.814Z
DELETE /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set/ps_mu9o9o6uybbit6th
       → 200 {"object":"sys_permission_set","id":"ps_mu9o9o6uybbit6th","success":true}
AFTER  : id=ps_mu9o9o6uybbit6th name=showcase_manager managed_by=package updated_at=2026-09-20T10:27:17.814Z
row still present: True · same id (not recreated): True · updated_at unchanged: True
```

The env-authored control under the identical call really deletes (18 rows to 17). **Both outcomes ship byte-identical envelopes**, so a UI cannot tell "deleted" from "no-op" — it will fire a success toast and show the row again on refresh. The **metadata door already ships the discriminator** for the same intent: `DELETE /api/v1/meta/permission/showcase_auditor` answers `{"success":true,"reset":false,"message":"No customization overlay found for permission/showcase_auditor — already at artifact default."}`.

**B — the duplicate-name refusal carries no `code` at all.**

```
POST /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set  {"name":"showcase_manager",…}  →  HTTP 409
{"error":"[Security] permission set 'showcase_manager' already exists","object":"sys_permission_set"}
```

Producer: `permission-set-projection.ts:1184` throws a bare `Error` with `.status = 409` and no `.code`; it runs **before** `assertPermissionSetNotPackageDeclared`, so an admin who types the base set's own name in the Clone dialog gets this, never `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. ADR-0112's 2026-08-17 amendment (#9232) makes this a contract question in so many words — 「**the flat door narrows too, so "every door" is literal**」, `packages/rest`'s flat `{ error, code }` responder must carry the closed member the status derives.

---

## Scope discipline

- ⛔ Nothing in `packages/plugins/plugin-security` was patched — that package is `domain:services`. **Findings A and B are handed to the dispatching seat to file in the owning lane**, with repro and dedupe words, per this executor's standing rule that a dev does not `POST /issues` itself. ⚠️ This is a stated conflict with the dispatch's `Writes:` line, which listed `POST /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues` as permitted; the executor's own contract forbids it and wins on conflict, so the conflict is named rather than silently resolved.
  - **A** — dedupe words: `sys_permission_set delete no-op` · `packaged permission set DELETE success true` · `data door delete reset discriminator` · `ADR-0094 delete reset not refused` · `permission set delete 200 unchanged`
  - **B** — dedupe words: `permission set already exists 409 no code` · `duplicate name refusal missing error code` · `ADR-0112 flat door code member` · `permission-set-projection 409 bare Error` · `clone dialog duplicate name code`
- ⛔ No label, assignee, ready-flip, enqueue or auto-merge was touched.
- No `packages/spec` change is needed for any of the three answers, so nothing was widened there.
- **Card body integrity: no sanitizer truncation found.** The body reads 4873 bytes through the API, ends with its dedupe-words block and its footer, and contains no less-than fragment that could have triggered a mutation.
